chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Ali ibn Asbat from some of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): In

the man who is behind the Imam and does not follow him, and the Imam precedes him in recitation, he said: 'If he has recited Umm al-Kitab, it suffices for him; he cuts off and bows.' And this report indicates that whenever he does not recite Fatihat al-Kitab, the prayer does not suffice for him, according to what we have presented earlier. And as for what was narrated:

key_terms.أُمَّ الْكِتَابِ: The Mother of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: The Opener of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)

ai.seo_question: What is the validity of prayer if the worshipper does not follow the Imam's recitation?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the validity of the follower's prayer when standing behind the Imam, specifically addressing the scenario where the Imam completes recitation before the follower. It underscores the Shia scholarly consensus that reciting *Al-Fatiha* is a mandatory pillar (*rukn*) for the individual worshipper, rendering the prayer invalid if omitted, regardless of the Imam's recitation style. This ruling highlights the distinct jurisprudential approach of the Ahl al-Bayt school regarding the independence of the follower's recitation in congregational prayers.
